week.worked: Monday night at Craven Cottage did the work: João Pedro eleven and Rogers eight, nineteen points from two Chelsea picks in a game he had been waiting a week for. Calafiori added nine at £5.5m. Fifty points, third of the five and seventh of eleven — a fair week that arrived four days late.
week.didnt: The expensive half of the squad. The armband on a £15.5m striker plus a £12.0m midfielder, Mbeumo and Shaw alongside them: four picks costing £40m, seven points between them, nine once the armband was counted. Kerkez played ninety minutes at Newcastle and returned nothing.
week.next: The United block is the whole question and it has just got more complicated in the right way: the midfield rebuild is finished at £155m, and the reporting says another left-back is expected before Tuesday without anyone at the club promising one. Ipswich at home on Friday is the fixture that either buys that block another month or ends it.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: He owns the two Chelsea players either side of him and not the one who outscored both. The calf flag has cleared and ownership has gone 11.7% to 14.0% in two days, which is the crowd arriving before he does.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: Nine points from City's left-back at exactly Kerkez's price. Kerkez is not the problem — Liverpool are shopping for wingers, not full-backs — so this is an upgrade rather than a rescue, and it can wait for a second team sheet.

week.worked: The cheap end held: Ajer eight at £4.5m and Schade three from a Brentford pair nobody else in the room owns, Szoboszlai eight, Calafiori nine, João Pedro eleven. Forty-nine points from a squad whose every worthwhile return came from £7.5m or less.
week.didnt: He put the armband on a United midfielder and the gloves on a United goalkeeper on the day United lost 2-0 at Hull: four from the captain, one from Lammens, two from Mbeumo. Ballard blanked, and eight points sat on the bench behind them.
week.next: One point behind Xabi and fifteen behind Le Professeur, which is nothing. His captain has just been voted PFA Player of the Year, which is a fact about last season and not about the sixteen shots worth under 0.1 xG apiece at Hull. The exposure to fix is the goalkeeper stacked on top of the outfield United players, and Ipswich at home is where that gets answered.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: He owns an Arsenal defender and no Arsenal attacker. Eleven points at £6.5m is the cheapest way to fix that, and the room has now gone a full week without anybody doing it.

watchlist.name: M.Sangaré
watchlist.note: A third Brentford asset, now £5.6m after a rise, and the one with the highest ceiling of the three. The case is the defensive-contribution rate repeating, not the fourteen on debut.

week.worked: The best mid-price spine of the five: Ndiaye nine, Szoboszlai eight, Rogers eight, Calafiori nine, João Pedro eleven — forty-five of his fifty-eight from five players priced between £5.5m and £7.5m. Fourth in the league, second of the five, and no chip spent.
week.didnt: Twelve points on the bench, nine of them Gvardiol, who started at left-back for City while Hume and Shaw kept their places in the eleven. It is the largest bench score in the room, and it is exactly the six points between him and first place with change left over.
week.next: The squad is right and the order is not. Nothing needs buying; the bench needed reading on Sunday afternoon rather than on Monday night. The one thing worth thinking about before Friday is whether a £4.5m Sunderland defender being played as a right winger is a defender at all.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: The only Arsenal asset he owns is a defender. At £6.5m the midfielder costs the same as E.Le Fée, who produced no shots and no chances created.

watchlist.name: De Cuyper
watchlist.note: Seventeen points at £4.6m and Brighton travel to a Chelsea side that has not kept a Premier League clean sheet in seventeen games. That is an argument for the attacking returns rather than for the seat, and one weekend is still one weekend.

week.worked: Two Arsenal picks nobody else in the room has — Havertz and Mosquera — returned twelve, Tzolis added six, Verbruggen kept a clean sheet at £4.5m and João Pedro brought eleven. Five players costing £31.5m made thirty-five of his forty-eight.
week.didnt: Semenyo, his second most expensive outfielder at £8.5m, returned two from a starting City wide role. Maguire was in the middle of the two set plays United conceded at Hull, and Greaves and Groß brought four between them. Forty-eight is last of the five, five behind the man in front of him.
week.next: Two of his four bench slots are effectively empty — one City defender at 0.8% ownership who was a substitute while a cheaper teammate played his position, and one Chelsea defender who has not made a competitive matchday squad. Neither cost him a point this week and both will cost him one the week a starter is flagged late.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: He has a Chelsea defender who has not played and no Chelsea midfielder. Thirteen points and the penalties at £9.5m is where that money belongs.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: The player who kept his own pick out of the City side, for exactly the same money. If a City defensive slot is worth holding, this is the one that starts.

week.worked: Sixty-four points, top of the five and second of eleven, six behind the leader. Rogers, Szoboszlai, Ndiaye, Calafiori and João Pedro made forty-five of it between them — five mid-price players rather than one lucky captain, which is the most repeatable week anybody had.
week.didnt: The Bench Boost, played in the first week of the season, returned six: two apiece from Kinsky, Diop and Groß and nothing from Konsa. His starting eleven scored fifty-eight, which is precisely Mr CR7's total. The chip is not decoration on the lead — the chip is the lead.
week.next: He leads on squad and on chip at once, and only one of those is repeatable. Two things to watch before Friday: whether the lead survives the first week somebody else has a chip and he does not, and whether Cash is startable at all, with Villa's record goalscorer expected to leave for Saudi Arabia, their goalkeeper asking to go and Arsenal at Villa Park.

watchlist.name: Ajer
watchlist.note: Eight points at exactly Cash's price, in a side that beat Spurs 3-0. The straight swap whenever Villa's week gets any worse, which it does most mornings.

watchlist.name: M.Sangaré
watchlist.note: A first half played one chip short wants cheap ceiling rather than cheap safety. This is the shape of that, if the defensive contributions hold up.

watchlist.name: Palmer
watchlist.note: Still the biggest collective miss of the opening weekend, and now the flag has cleared too: thirteen points, Chelsea's penalties, a goal and an assist, and not one of the five owns him. Ownership has moved 11.7% to 14.0% while the room stood still.

watchlist.name: Ødegaard
watchlist.note: Eleven points at £6.5m. Four of the five own an Arsenal defender and none owns the midfielder. This was written a gameweek ago, is still true, and has stopped being an oversight.

watchlist.name: Gvardiol
watchlist.note: Nine points from City's left-back. One of the five has the right City defender and left him on the bench; another has the wrong one at 0.8% ownership. Same club, same price, opposite outcomes.

watchlist.name: Gakpo
watchlist.note: Twelve points at £7.0m and under 6% owned, and the risk has flipped. Last week it was that he might be sold; this week Liverpool have had two bids for a winger rejected, moved on to a second and are talking to a third, and want two of them signed by Tuesday.

watchlist.name: Welbeck
watchlist.note: With one Chelsea striker sold to Forest for £50m and another in talks with Villa, the reporting has him as the second of Alonso's two. A £6.0m forward at 1% ownership behind a nailed £7.5m one is a lottery ticket, not a pick — worth naming, not worth buying.

watchlist.name: Woltemade
watchlist.note: Newcastle's penalty taker in front of the kindest six-game run on the ticker, and a substitute in the only game so far. The fixtures have been the case for two weeks; the team sheet still is not.

verdicts.name: Palmer
verdicts.why: Thirteen points, the penalties and the calf flag now cleared to fully fit — the best midfield return of the weekend, owned by none of the five and by 14% of the game.
verdicts.trigger: Two games spent wide rather than at ten, or the calf returning.

verdicts.name: João Pedro
verdicts.why: Eleven points, a new deal to 2034 and the number nine shirt, and with one strike partner sold to Forest and another in talks with Villa the minutes are no longer contested.
verdicts.trigger: Two Chelsea games without a shot in the box, and 67% ownership becomes the risk rather than the floor.

verdicts.name: Rogers
verdicts.why: Tapped in on debut after a club-record move and got the full ninety, in a Chelsea midfield currently missing Caicedo and possibly about to lose Enzo to City.
verdicts.trigger: A week wide or on the bench once Chelsea's central midfield is whole again.

verdicts.name: Sánchez
verdicts.why: Two errors leading to goals at Fulham, a club that has not kept a Premier League clean sheet in seventeen games, and a manager who was asked about him again before the cup tie rather than being allowed to move on.
verdicts.trigger: Chelsea getting through the window without signing a goalkeeper, plus two clean sheets.

verdicts.name: Martinez
verdicts.why: A £5.0m goalkeeper at 4.1% ownership who has told his club he wants to leave, was not in the squad for the opener with Bizot picked ahead of him, and whose replacement was signed for £30m this month.
verdicts.trigger: The window shutting on Tuesday with him still at Villa and back between the posts.

verdicts.name: Enzo
verdicts.why: City are expected to lodge a formal offer before Tuesday at a price Chelsea set at £120m, and he started the opener on the bench behind a makeshift pairing.
verdicts.trigger: The deadline passing with him at Chelsea and starting in central midfield.

verdicts.name: Palestra
verdicts.why: Left out of the matchday squad altogether for the opener with a setback, and now carrying a 75% flag without having played a competitive minute.
verdicts.trigger: One competitive start. Until then a £5.5m defender with no debut is a slot rather than a player.

verdicts.name: Lacroix
verdicts.why: Six points at £6.0m from a back line that conceded twice, in a team on a seventeen-game run without a Premier League clean sheet — the longest since 1991.
verdicts.trigger: A clean sheet against Brighton. Until one arrives, every Chelsea defender is an attacking punt at defender prices.

verdicts.name: Welbeck
verdicts.why: Reported as the second of Alonso's two strikers now that Delap has gone to Forest for £50m and Jackson is in talks with Villa, at £6.0m and 1% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: A start with João Pedro rested, or Chelsea signing a forward before Tuesday, which ends it.

verdicts.name: Gonzalo
verdicts.why: Scored on his Fulham debut, has the penalties, and costs £6.0m at 3.1% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: Anyone starting ahead of him once Fulham's forwards are all available.

verdicts.name: King
verdicts.why: Nineteen, Fulham's best player on the night by a distance, the near-post equaliser and a shot from range that nearly made it 3-3, at £5.5m and 0.4% ownership.
verdicts.trigger: Two games without ninety minutes. A teenager's breakout night is a night.

verdicts.name: Haaland
verdicts.why: Two points, ninety minutes, the penalties and the armband from three of the five — a blank that separated nobody, and City have spent the week selling the forwards behind him rather than buying one.
verdicts.trigger: A serious injury, or three straight weeks of City creating through the wide players and past him.

verdicts.name: B.Fernandes
verdicts.why: PFA Player of the Year on Tuesday, and sixteen of United's twenty-one shots at Hull worth under 0.1 expected goals apiece on Saturday. The award is about last season; the shot map is about this one.
verdicts.trigger: A blank at home to Ipswich with the same shot profile, and £12.0m stops being a price and starts being a hole.

verdicts.name: Mbeumo
verdicts.why: Two points, and the Hull post-mortem points at shot quality rather than at the two set plays — the slower problem, not the quicker one.
verdicts.trigger: United blanking at home to Ipswich, which makes the GW4 sale automatic.

verdicts.name: Shaw
verdicts.why: Thirty-one, started all thirty-eight league games last season and all but one of United's last forty-four, and the reporting is that another left-back is expected before Tuesday in front of a season with almost no free midweeks.
verdicts.trigger: A left-back arriving before the deadline, or one week out of the side. Either ends a £4.5m pick whose entire case is that he never misses.

verdicts.name: Lammens
verdicts.why: Cheap is not the same as safe behind a defence that lost at Hull to two headers.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in the next three, or enough save points to make the floor worth it.

verdicts.name: Maguire
verdicts.why: One point, and he is the defender in the middle of the set plays United conceded.
verdicts.trigger: Losing his place when United's other centre-backs are fit.

verdicts.name: Amad
verdicts.why: Flagged at 75%, with a report that he could be out for up to six weeks and a club declining to clarify either way.
verdicts.trigger: A confirmed return date, or a start. A £6.0m midfielder whose club will not say what is wrong is unownable.

verdicts.name: Šeško
verdicts.why: Zero pre-season minutes became twenty-three at Hull, and the start still has not come.
verdicts.trigger: A start plus a goal and he re-enters as a watch — not before.

verdicts.name: Calafiori
verdicts.why: Nine points, owned by four of the five and by 41% of the game — still the closest thing to a free lunch on the list.
verdicts.trigger: A recurrence of the knee trouble that has followed him around.

verdicts.name: Ødegaard
verdicts.why: Eleven points at £6.5m and a week later still nobody in the room owns him, which has stopped being an oversight and become a choice.
verdicts.trigger: A repeat of last season's injury record, or Arsenal's returns concentrating in Saka and Gyökeres instead.

verdicts.name: Saka
verdicts.why: Nine points and Arsenal's penalties at £9.5m, with barely 10% of the game on him.
verdicts.trigger: The recurring hamstring, or rotation through the Champions League weeks.

verdicts.name: Havertz
verdicts.why: Six points at £7.5m and 7.1% ownership, in a forward line that has not yet settled around Gyökeres.
verdicts.trigger: Two weeks as a substitute once Arsenal's attack is fully fit.

verdicts.name: Mosquera
verdicts.why: Six points deputising while both Saliba and Timber are out with no return date — the points are real, the seat is borrowed.
verdicts.trigger: Saliba's back clearing. When it does, this pick ends.

verdicts.name: White
verdicts.why: Eleven points, the highest of any Arsenal defender, at £5.5m and 6.1% ownership — and the reason is the same injury list that put Mosquera in the side.
verdicts.trigger: Timber's groin clearing, which returns him to a rotation option at a starter's price.

verdicts.name: Tzolis
verdicts.why: Six points and a debut that got noticed; a quarter of the game is on him now and the price has not moved.
verdicts.trigger: Saka and Rice fully fit squeezing the minutes.

verdicts.name: Szoboszlai
verdicts.why: Central midfield at Newcastle and on Liverpool's penalties at £7.0m, but he made zero tackles and won three of ten duels there, and the man brought on to steady it did more in half an hour.
verdicts.trigger: Mac Allister starting in the pivot, or a shift back to right-back. Either halves the appeal.

verdicts.name: Gravenberch
verdicts.why: Lost the ball for both Newcastle goals, and his manager's public answer was that the problem is not personnel — which is either loyalty or a plan, and the transfer priority being wingers suggests a plan.
verdicts.trigger: Liverpool signing a holding midfielder by Tuesday, or one week out of the two-man pivot.

verdicts.name: Gakpo
verdicts.why: Twelve points at £7.0m, and Liverpool have had two bids for a right-sided winger rejected, moved on to a second target and are talking to a third, with two signings wanted before Tuesday.
verdicts.trigger: The window shutting with no wide forward arriving. Then he is a buy rather than a maybe.

verdicts.name: Kerkez
verdicts.why: Ninety minutes at left-back at Newcastle in a 2-2, and Liverpool's remaining window money is earmarked for wide attackers rather than full-backs.
verdicts.trigger: One week on the bench, or Liverpool moving to a back three, and £5.5m stops making sense.

verdicts.name: Gvardiol
verdicts.why: Started at left-back and returned nine — the City defensive seat that actually exists at £5.5m.
verdicts.trigger: O'Reilly reclaiming the left side once Doku is back on 5 September.

verdicts.name: Aït-Nouri
verdicts.why: A substitute at the Etihad with Gvardiol at left-back, 0.8% owned, and still occupying a bench slot in this league.
verdicts.trigger: One start ahead of Gvardiol. Same price, same club, and only one of them plays.

verdicts.name: Guéhi
verdicts.why: Ten points on his first City start, in a back line reshuffled around an injury rather than by design.
verdicts.trigger: One week out of the XI with City's other centre-backs fit and £6.0m is wrong.

verdicts.name: Cherki
verdicts.why: Eight points from the bench, and City have now loaned Marmoush to Spurs with an obligation to buy — the queue in front of him is shorter than it was on Saturday.
verdicts.trigger: A start. The trigger set three weeks ago has not changed and still has not been met.

verdicts.name: Semenyo
verdicts.why: Two points at £8.5m from a starting City wide role. Marmoush leaving makes the minutes safer; it does not make the price right.
verdicts.trigger: Two more blanks with Cherki getting the minutes instead, and this is a sack.

verdicts.name: Marmoush
verdicts.why: A loan to Spurs agreed with an obligation to buy at £60m, which turns a £7.0m fourth-choice City forward into a possible starter somewhere — for a side whose manager says it is not a team yet.
verdicts.trigger: A completed medical and a start. Until both, he is a City player who was an unused substitute.

verdicts.name: M.Sangaré
verdicts.why: Fourteen on debut and a price rise to £5.6m, but the case is the defensive-contribution rate rather than the two assists, one of which was a parried shot.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks over the threshold and he is the cheap midfielder of the season. One is a debut.

verdicts.name: Ajer
verdicts.why: Eight points at £4.5m in a Brentford side whose press left Spurs without a shot on target until 3-0 down.
verdicts.trigger: Kayode taking the aerial returns instead, or one rotation.

verdicts.name: Schade
verdicts.why: A game-high five second-half shots and a penalty won in a 3-0 — the underlying numbers are ahead of the three points.
verdicts.trigger: Two more weeks of shot volume without a return and the finishing becomes the story.

verdicts.name: Thiago
verdicts.why: Missed from the spot after converting ten of his previous eleven, blanked in a 3-0 win, and Brentford's run turns hard from GW5.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties to anyone, and £8.0m is a sack the same day.

verdicts.name: Calvert-Lewin
verdicts.why: Leeds play through him and he started; a one-point opener is a dull floor, which is what he was bought for.
verdicts.trigger: Losing the penalties, or a striker arriving before the window shuts.

verdicts.name: Ndiaye
verdicts.why: Nine points on Everton's penalties at £6.0m in a side that opened with a clean sheet; two of the five have him.
verdicts.trigger: Everton's fixtures turning, or the penalty duty moving.

verdicts.name: Dewsbury-Hall
verdicts.why: Ninety minutes and the opener in a 2-0 from a £6.5m central midfielder in a side keeping clean sheets.
verdicts.trigger: A second blank in three with Everton conceding, and he goes back to being a hedge.

verdicts.name: Verbruggen
verdicts.why: A clean sheet in a 4-0 at £4.5m, which is the entire job description of this pick.
verdicts.trigger: Steele getting a cup start that turns into a league one.

verdicts.name: Kinsky
verdicts.why: Spurs did not have a shot on target until 3-0 down, and their manager said afterwards that they are not a team yet — while the club kept spending, past £312m this summer.
verdicts.trigger: Reassess at GW7 — window shut, players settled, fixtures softer. Until then this is a bench goalkeeper.

verdicts.name: Cash
verdicts.why: Minus one in a 4-0, and the week since has brought a goalkeeper asking to leave, a record goalscorer expected in Saudi Arabia and bids going out for two replacements. Arsenal at Villa Park is next.
verdicts.trigger: Two clean sheets in three, or the window closing with the dressing room settled.

verdicts.name: Watkins
verdicts.why: Now reported as expected to join Al-Hilal, with Villa in talks over one replacement and an offer already lodged for another.
verdicts.trigger: The deadline passing with him at Villa and in the starting eleven.

verdicts.name: Mateta
verdicts.why: The subject of a Villa offer that falls well below Palace's valuation, from a manager who says publicly he wants to keep him.
verdicts.trigger: Tuesday passing with him at Palace. A £6.5m forward with the penalties and settled minutes is then worth a look.

verdicts.name: Hume
verdicts.why: Sunderland pushed him forward into a right-wing role — good for assists, bad for the clean sheets he was bought for.
verdicts.trigger: A second week out of the back line. A £4.5m defender who does not defend is priced wrong for the position.

verdicts.name: E.Le Fée
verdicts.why: Plenty of the ball and Sunderland going through him, but no shots and no chances created at £6.0m.
verdicts.trigger: A return in the next two, or the money goes to a midfielder who takes shots.

verdicts.name: Emersonn
verdicts.why: Nine points and the best underlying attacking numbers of any Ipswich player at £5.5m — a genuinely cheap forward with a role.
verdicts.trigger: One start on the bench once Ipswich's attacking signings settle.

verdicts.name: Igor Jesus
verdicts.why: Forest have agreed a club-record £50m for a striker, which is not a fee a club pays for a substitute.
verdicts.trigger: Keeping the shirt for two starts once the new man is registered.

verdicts.name: Woltemade
verdicts.why: Newcastle's £6.0m penalty taker in front of the best six-game run on the ticker, and a substitute in the one game so far — with the man who started ahead of him now carrying a knock.
verdicts.trigger: One start. The fixtures have been the case for two weeks and the team sheet still is not.

signals.text: Chelsea have not kept a Premier League clean sheet in seventeen games, their longest run since August 1991, and conceded twice again at Fulham. The manager was asked about his goalkeeper again before the cup tie rather than being allowed to move on, and the club are weighing an experienced replacement who has become available.
signals.action: price every Chelsea defender as an attacking punt until a clean sheet actually arrives — the fixture list looks kind and the back line has not earned it

signals.text: Their goalkeeper has told the club he wants to leave, was left out of the squad at Brighton with Bizot picked instead and Suzuki — a £30m signing this month — on the bench, and Chelsea are now in talks with his representatives. Their record Premier League goalscorer is expected to join Al-Hilal. They have opened talks for one striker at £65m and lodged a below-valuation offer for another.
signals.action: no Villa asset is startable in GW2, and the cheap defenders are not the safe part — the whole spine is being rebuilt while Arsenal come to Villa Park

signals.text: Liverpool had bids of £50m and £60m for Brighton's Yankuba Minteh rejected, have switched attention to Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr, and are still in talks with Paris St-Germain over Bradley Barcola. The club want two wide attackers signed before Tuesday's deadline.
signals.action: twelve points and 5.5% ownership is the right shape of bet at the wrong moment. Wait for Tuesday night, then buy or forget it

signals.text: He lost the ball for both goals at Newcastle — the first eleven seconds before Elanga scored, the second on a back heel at the edge of the box. Iraola: "I think it's just not personnel. I understand you are telling me basically that Ryan Gravenberch is the six and he is on the edge of the box — but if he shoots and he scores we are saying what a play from Ryan Gravenberch." Mac Allister came on and made two tackles and won four of five duels in half an hour.
signals.action: the manager is defending the selection, but Liverpool's spending priority is wingers, so nothing is being fixed this week — treat every Liverpool midfielder's floor as lower than the fixtures suggest

signals.text: The Baleba signing completes a £155m midfield rebuild and turns attention to left-back. He is thirty-one, started all thirty-eight league games last season and all but one of United's last forty-four, and had a poor injury record before that forty-game season gave him a week between matches. If United get through two cup rounds they have no free midweek until Christmas. Most expect another left-back before Tuesday, though the club are stressing caution.
signals.action: a £4.5m defender whose whole case is that he never misses is exactly the pick a squad signing and a fixture crush break. Read the deadline, not the price

signals.text: United are choosing to offer no clarification on the extent of his injury amid a report that he could be out for up to six weeks. It is also the reason a Zirkzee sale to Serie A has stalled.
signals.action: a 75% flag with a six-week rumour behind it and no club statement is a nought waiting to happen

signals.text: City are expected to submit a formal offer before the deadline, having been told to pay £120m by 14 August and let the date pass. Alonso, asked whether he would feature against Luton: "Yes, we expect that he's involved. He's trained, he's training really well, he's a good professional and he will be involved." He started the league opener on the bench, with Reece James and Lavia in central midfield.
signals.action: still a hold at £7.0m. A midfielder being selected while his club negotiates a nine-figure sale is not a seat you can plan around

signals.text: Spurs have agreed a loan with an obligation to buy at £60m next summer, with a medical in the coming days. He started only eight league games last season for around 700 minutes, and was an unused substitute in City's opener.
signals.action: the interesting half is what it does to City rather than to Spurs — the queue behind Haaland is now one shorter, which is the case for Cherki finally getting a start

signals.text: The midfield has been rebuilt twice over in one window: Rodri to Barcelona for £65m, Reijnders to Al-Qadsiah for £52m, Nico González to Newcastle for £52m, against Elliot Anderson at £116m and Bouaddi at £86m. Two forwards have left for Spurs in three days.
signals.action: nobody's City minutes are safe to project from one team sheet — including the ones that produced the weekend's cheap defensive haul

signals.text: Forest have agreed a club-record £50m — £45m plus £5m in add-ons — for a striker their manager made a priority target, with the deal done before the deadline.
signals.action: Forest's existing forwards go from starters to cover overnight. Anyone holding one at £6.0m is holding a substitute

signals.text: Liverpool have been linked with a bid, denied by both clubs. Palace manager Pierre Sage: "For the moment, yes [I expect him to stay], because when you have three years on the contract it is not easy to leave... He is injured and maybe you can make a link between his injury and the situation. But for me, he is honest and I have no problem with that."
signals.action: a groin injury with no return date and a manager publicly linking the injury to the transfer talk. Nothing to own here before Tuesday

signals.text: Past £312m spent this summer, with a £75m winger and a forward on loan with a £60m obligation both arriving from City this week, on top of four debutants who started at Brentford in a 3-0 defeat with no shot on target until 3-0 down. De Zerbi: "I think we are not a team yet, for a lot of reasons."
signals.action: target Spurs rather than own them until the window shuts and the fixtures soften around GW7 — the squad is still being assembled in public

signals.text: The post-mortem on the 2-0 at Hull puts the problem somewhere other than the set pieces: twenty-one shots, sixteen of them worth under 0.1 expected goals apiece — the same pattern as last season, when United had the third-worst average open-play shot quality of any top-half club.
signals.source: Andrew Beasley, via the touchline digest of 2026-08-25
signals.action: this is the slower problem, not the quicker one. Set-piece goals stop; bad shots do not. Ipswich at home is the test

signals.text: The focus before Tuesday is outgoings: one striker sold to Forest for £50m, another valued at £65m in talks with Villa, and a squad that still carried thirty-nine senior players a week ago. Mudryk, Essugo and Marc Guiu were all left out of the squad entirely for the opener.
signals.action: Chelsea team sheets are being written by the window as much as by form until Tuesday night

doctrine.text: Rank insurance is a real cost — price the drift on every call.
New-manager minutes are unknowable until three XIs.
Champions' template assets are default-own; passing needs a priced case.
Opening weekend prices nothing. A promoted side beating a giant is one result until the same shape holds twice — sell on a pattern, never on a scoreline.
A cheap-defender haul is a match, not a seat. Before buying points that already happened, check the player is still fit and still first choice.

Grade a chip against its own median week — and then check the table before saying it did not matter. Six points from a Bench Boost is a chip spent rather than used; it is also, exactly, the six points between first of the five and second.

Buy the line-up, not the scoreboard. Three of the weekend's best mid-price returns came from players who started on a bench or out of position, and two of the room's bench slots are held by players who have not been in a matchday eleven.

A player the whole room passed on is a bigger exposure than a player the whole room owns. All five owned Haaland and João Pedro; none owned Palmer, who outscored both. Check the consensus blind spot before checking the consensus pick.

An open window is a team-sheet risk, not a shopping opportunity. In the six days before this deadline a first-choice goalkeeper stopped being selected, a record goalscorer stopped training with the group, a City forward was loaned out, and Liverpool bid twice for a winger who would take a squad player's place. Buy after the window shuts, not into it.

roast.text: Le Professeur leads the five by six points. His Bench Boost, played in the first week of the season, returned six points. His starting eleven scored fifty-eight, which to the point is exactly what Mr CR7 scored without spending anything at all. So the entire lead is a chip that this page graded, on Monday, as "spent rather than used" — a chip so wasteful it is currently the only thing keeping him top. Congratulations, one supposes. Meanwhile this page spent yesterday explaining, in some detail, that two of The Special One's eleven had never appeared on a pitch. They were on his bench. The machine wrote three sentences of analysis about a decision he did not make, and has since gone back and read the squad file it was looking at the whole time.

plan.outlook: Gameweek 1 is settled and nothing on the pitch has moved since Monday: Le Professeur 64 and second of eleven, Mr CR7 58, Xabi 50, Sir Fergie 49, The Special One 48, with Gunners.exe out in front on 70. Sixteen points cover the five, which is one bench ordering. What has moved is the market, and all of it lands before Friday's deadline and Tuesday's window close. Villa are being taken apart — a goalkeeper who wants out and was not selected, a record goalscorer expected in Saudi Arabia, bids going out for two replacements — with Arsenal at Villa Park in GW2. Liverpool have had two bids rejected for a winger and are chasing two more, which is the question hanging over the room's cheapest good idea. United have finished a £155m midfield and turned to the left-back position one of the five is invested in at £4.5m. City have loaned out a forward and rebuilt the midfield twice over. None of that argues for a transfer this week: the buys that stand up — Palmer, Ødegaard, Gvardiol — are the same three that stood up a week ago and cost the same money, and everything else on the board is either one game old or in the middle of a move. The three real decisions are unchanged: the United block at Old Trafford in GW4, whether anybody in this room ever buys an Arsenal midfielder, and whether a second chip gets spent in August.

chips.note: First-half chips die at the GW19 deadline (2 Jan). A good week used beats a perfect week hoarded — but Gameweek 1, with every squad fifteen fit players and no doubles anywhere, is neither. One of the five found that out for six points. The uncomfortable footnote, which this page got wrong on Monday and is correcting now: those six points are his entire lead.

log.call: Day-0 squad: Haaland (C) vs BOU; bets on Palmer, Kerkez, Hume; passed on Bruno Fernandes at £12.0m with Mbeumo/Shaw/Lammens carrying the Man Utd run.

Held again with GW1 unfinished: no transfer, the free one banked to Friday, all three United men kept into Ipswich at home. Haaland (C) at Selhurst Park, B.Fernandes vice, 3-4-3 unchanged. Declined the Hull £4.0m defenders after their haul.

No move with Gameweek 1 one fixture from finished. Declined all three of the weekend's obvious buys — the Hull £4.0m defenders (all flagged at 75%), Sangaré's fourteen on debut, and Cherki's eight off the bench — on the grounds that a doubt or a substitute is not a seat. Graded Le Professeur's Gameweek 1 Bench Boost as spent rather than used at six points, while conceding he leads the five without it.

Settled Gameweek 1 at fifty points and fifth of eleven. Upgraded Palmer to nailed after thirteen on the opening night and named him, with Ødegaard, as the room's shape rather than its luck — neither is owned by any of the five. Sacked Palestra and Aït-Nouri as slots rather than players after both missed their clubs' matchday elevens, and sacked Cash and Watkins on Villa's week rather than on Villa's fixture. Recommended no transfer before Friday: every obvious buy is either one game old, flagged, or in the middle of a transfer.

No transfer recommended for the third run running, two days before the deadline and six before the window shuts — on the explicit grounds that an open window is a team-sheet risk rather than a shopping opportunity (D9). Downgraded Shaw on the reporting that United expect another left-back before Tuesday. Flipped the Gakpo case: the risk is no longer that Liverpool sell him but that they buy over him, with two bids rejected for one winger and two more targets live. Sacked Villa's goalkeeper as a slot, and Forest's incumbent striker on a £50m arrival. Corrected two errors of our own from Monday: The Special One's dead men were on his bench, not in his eleven, and Le Professeur's six-point Bench Boost is not a footnote to his lead, it is the whole of it.
